title: Code snippet reveal (9:16)
description: A 15-second code reveal rendered in the browser with no external tools: an editor window types the snippet with a human rhythm and syntax highlighting (Python, JavaScript, Rust or Bash), the key line lights up while the rest dims, a terminal panel shows what the program prints, and the title gives way to a takeaway. The code is displayed, never executed. Code-rendered (scene.code-snippet).

title.description: What the snippet shows, under 40 characters (e.g. 'Count words in one line')

filename.description: A plausible file name with the language's extension and no spaces (e.g. main.py, app.js, main.rs, backup.sh)

code.description: The code as one string with a line break between lines and indentation as leading spaces: 3 to 12 lines of at most 40 characters each. It must be correct, idiomatic and do exactly what the brief describes; no placeholder lines

key_line.description: The single most important line of the code, copied character for character from it: one line only, no line breaks (it is highlighted)

output.description: What running the code prints, exactly as this code would print it (no added quotes): 1 to 4 lines of at most 40 characters, separated by line breaks

takeaway.description: Closing line a viewer should remember, under 56 characters; no claims the brief does not make

look.description: Editor look: midnight (navy, blue accent), paper (light editor, dark terminal), terminal (black, green phosphor), ember (warm dark, orange)

energy.description: Mood of the procedural lo-fi bed

scene.description: The code animation; rendered from the slots unless supplied

music.description: Music bed; produced procedurally unless a cleared track is supplied

click.description: Soft click as the key line lights up

whoosh.description: Whoosh as the terminal slides up

copy_examples.brief: Short for JavaScript beginners: remove duplicates from an array by spreading a Set. Show that [3, 1, 3, 2, 1] becomes [3, 1, 2]. Takeaway: a Set keeps only the first copy of each value.

inputs.title: Remove duplicates with a Set
inputs.takeaway: A Set keeps only the first copy of each value

copy_examples.note: The code does exactly what the brief asks and nothing more; the key line is copied from the code; the output is what Node prints for that array; the takeaway restates the brief's point.

style.typography: Inter ExtraBold title; JetBrains Mono or DejaVu Sans Mono code

direction.action: Window scales in, code types with a human rhythm, key line lights up, terminal runs, takeaway replaces the title

notes: The animation is code (recipes/scene/code-snippet); the content model supplies the title, file name, language, code lines, key line, output lines and takeaway. Code and output are displayed as text and never executed.

The code font shrinks to fit the longest line but never below about 2.6% of the short side; longer lines fail the render. Keep lines under 40 characters and 12 lines. The key line must appear in the code or the render fails.

Beats at 15 s with output and a takeaway: typing 1.0-8.4 s, key line at 8.65 s (frame 259), terminal at 10.25 s (frame 307), takeaway at 12.4 s (frame 372). Sound is cued to those frames: a soft click on the highlight, a quiet whoosh as the terminal rises and a swell under the takeaway.

quality_gates.description: Integrated loudness lands within 1 LU of the -14 LUFS delivery target.
Decoded true peak stays at or below -0.5 dBTP after AAC encoding.
No stretch of blank picture (no visible contrast, any colour) lasts longer than 0.5 seconds.
A developer confirms the code is correct for the stated language, does what the title says, and that the terminal output is exactly what it prints.
